eli5.text: When you press Ctrl+C in the command-line tool, the program now stops right away instead of making you press it twice and waiting to confirm. If you looked at the terminal while using the CLI, you'd see that pressing Ctrl+C once immediately ends your session without any warning message or countdown. The same update also switched the Markdown renderer to produce plain text with visible code blocks (surrounded by backticks) and headers prefixed with # symbols, removing the previous rich-text formatting and stopping the tool from depending on React for that rendering step.

A 15-minute timeout guard limits the duration of the debug session.

eli5.text: When a release build of the toolkit fails, the build system now automatically opens a live debug terminal so a developer can ssh in and investigate what went wrong in real time. The door to that terminal stays open for at most fifteen minutes, after which the session closes on its own. The rest of the build process continues unchanged.

eli5.text: When you publish a new version of the software kit, the release process now accepts a list of custom setting names and values that should be turned on for that specific build. The step that prepares and publishes the production version now automatically passes two of those settings so the kit behaves like it is running in the production environment, including pointing it at the live backend address. A temporary hold on extra changes was also moved to an earlier part of the process so it no longer gets in the way when the version number is updated, and the old shortcut that opened a live debugging session was removed.

eli5.text: The internal tool that builds and releases the programmer's kit (that's the "SDK") now accepts an optional set of custom settings that override its normal defaults when someone starts it up manually. These custom settings are handed over as a block of text, so a person triggering the release can swap in their own values for things like API endpoints or flags without touching the underlying setup. Nothing changes for automated runs, which stick to their original configuration; only manual or specially triggered runs can take advantage of this new override. It's a small addition, just a few lines, and it's live today but only useful to whoever is running those controlled release builds.

ai.title: Fix SDK release workflow ordering
ai.summary: Reorders `build-and-publish-sdk` to run after `prepare-and-commit-prod` in `.github/workflows/sdk-release-prod.yml`. Resolves race condition where SDK build triggered before version commit/push. Ensures `sdk/package.json` updates persist before artifact generation.

eli5.text: When the team releases a new version of their software kit, the automated publishing process runs in the correct order now. Previously, the code that builds the kit and makes it available was triggered before the version number was properly saved and sent to the servers, which could lead to confusion. Now that version update is committed first, ensuring the published kit always reflects the right version. This affects the internal release process and should make software kit releases more reliable.

The terminal's text and markdown formatting has been rewritten to produce cleaner, simpler plain-text output that reads more naturally. Behind the scenes, the release build process has been reorganized so that new versions are published to users only after the version number is safely committed, making releases more reliable. Additionally, developers troubleshooting release builds can now access an interactive SSH debug shell if a build step fails, helping fix problems faster. These changes make quitting the tool smoother, output easier to read, and the release pipeline more dependable for everyone.

eli5.text: A new planning assistant has been added to the internal agent system that helps decide what to do next in a conversation. Before each action, it trims down the accumulated conversation history to keep things focused, then asks two different thinking helpers (one powered by a model from Anthropic, one from OpenAI) to each suggest a possible next move. The suggestions are used purely as inspiration; the new assistant writes its own real next step based on them, then those draft ideas are cleaned out of the message history so only the final step remains visible.

eli5.text: The database lookup path that powers your agent runs and message cost tracking has been switched back to a shared location, so all parts of the backend now pull from the same source again. If you were poking around the code, you'd see backend files importing from '@codebuff/common/db' instead of the 'internal' folder. This also tidies up a handful of agent definitions and the editor settings file, but it won't change what you see on screen.

ai.title: Fix Stripe import path in backend tests
ai.summary: Updated Stripe import path in `backend/src/__tests__/auto-topup.test.ts` from `@codebuff/common/util/stripe` to `@codebuff/internal/util/stripe`. Corrects module resolution failure during test execution. Scope limited to backend test suite.

eli5.text: The team moved a reference in the backend's test code so that the test suite points to the correct place where the Stripe payment helper actually lives. This fixes a failure that was stopping the backend tests from running at all, so the test results you see will now be accurate instead of erroring out. Nothing about how payments work for you changed, only whether the behind-the-scenes checks that verify payments behave correctly will run successfully.

ai.title: Upgrade drizzle-kit to 0.31.6
ai.summary: Bump drizzle-kit from 0.28.1 to 0.31.6 in common/package.json. Keeps drizzle-orm pinned at 0.36.4. Internal dependency update.

eli5.text: The database setup tool used internally by the development environment has been upgraded to a newer version. This is behind-the-scenes maintenance that affects only developers working on the codebase; regular users will not notice any difference. If you looked at the project files, you would see that one line referencing the tool's version number has changed from the older version to the newer one. The change is live today in the development branch, alongside several other internal adjustments to the release process.

ai.title: drizzle-kit 0.28.1
ai.summary: Revert drizzle-kit 0.31.6 to 0.28.1. Affects common/package.json. Pins 0.28.1.

eli5.text: The database helper tool used while building apps has been switched back from its newest version to an older one, so any features that depended on the newer version will stop working and builders may see new warnings or errors when starting up. This is live today for anyone who runs the build tools in this shared code workspace.
